newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA mandated for Sanwa MTN programme.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA mandated for Sanwa MTN programme.

text.p: The Commonwealth Bank of Australia said on Monday it had been formally mandated as arranger to a A$500 million medium term note programme for Sanwa Australia Ltd, a unit of The Sanwa Bank Ltd of Japan.
The programme will allow Sanwa Australia to issue a variety of different debt instruments for terms between one and 10 years and will be guaranteed by Sanwa Bank of Japan.
Wayne Hoy, CBA's Chief Manager Financial Markets, said the programme is another milestone for Australian capital markets.

"This is the first time that a Japanese entity has established a medium tern note programme in the Australian market, confirming that sophisticated international borrowers have a high level of confidence in Australia's capital markets," Hoy said in a statement.
"The programme also reaffirms the Commonwealth Bank's position as the leading arranger/lead manager of domestic debt securities," Hoy said.
CBA and Sanwa Australia will be dealers on the programme with the remainder of the dealer panel formed in due course.

"We expect further expansion in our corporate banking activities in Australia. This programme will provide stable funding, whilst also offering the opportunity to diversify the funding of these activities," said Yukio Kakubari, Sanwa Australia's General manager of Treasury.
Sanwa Australia is the third largest bank in the world by total assets and is rated Aa3 by Moody's Investors Service.
